* 1. execute
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: executor/execute
:FILE: src/graphden/executor/interface.clj
:LINE: 72
:MINS: 2.8
:END:

Graphden puts composition in stored data and small operations in Clojure. For example, ~{:name :three :parent :add :args {:nums [1 2]}}~ describes a function returning 3; it does not define a Clojure function body. It inherits ~:add~'s ~:nums~ slot and binds that slot to two list items. The stored form has a ~fn~ row, a ~binding~ row targeting the inherited slot, and two ~binding-list-item~ rows. The parent's ~fn-slot~ links its function to the immutable slot. See the existing arithmetic examples in [[file:../../../resources/packages/core/tests/fns.edn][core.tests]].

The executor compiles this description into a callable Clojure function. References prepare deferred inputs: an ~:if~ implementation reads only its selected branch, so the other branch does not run. Defaults and composition belong in ~fns.edn~; add an ~impls.clj~ primitive when an operation needs a host library or runtime facility. This keeps dependencies visible instead of hiding a pipeline inside one implementation.

~execute~ accepts an [[file:glossary.org::#term/context][execution context]], a [[file:glossary.org::#term/graph-function][graph function]] ID (~fn-id~), and named [[file:glossary.org::#term/free-argument][free arguments]]. The context determines which storage and branch the call sees. This public entry validates the argument map and delegates execution to ~compile-runtime~.

* 2. execute
:PROPERTIES:

:FILE: src/graphden/executor/compile_runtime.clj

Runs a previously compiled [[file:glossary.org::#term/graph-function][graph function]]. It first checks cancellation and any configured execution-permission guard, then binds the [[file:glossary.org::#term/effect][allowed effects]] for the call. The [[file:glossary.org::#term/compiled-registry][compiled registry]] maps function IDs to [[file:glossary.org::#term/closure][closures]]: callable Clojure functions retaining their prepared dependencies. ~execute~ looks up the [[file:glossary.org::#term/closure][closure]], translates named input into slot-ID and name keys, and calls ~(closure translated ctx)~.

Loads the graph cache while protecting concurrent writes. Before reading storage, the loader records the [[file:glossary.org::#term/invalidation][invalidation]] [[file:glossary.org::#term/invalidation][epoch]], a counter incremented when data changes. It installs its result under a lock only if that counter is unchanged; otherwise an older read could overwrite the graph installed by a newer write.

* 5. registry
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: executor/registry
:FILE: src/graphden/executor/compile_runtime.clj
:LINE: 1049
:MINS: 2.8
:END:

Returns the [[file:glossary.org::#term/compiled-registry][compiled registry]], a map from function IDs to Clojure [[file:glossary.org::#term/closure][closures]]. An existing registry can be served while a background rebuild refreshes it. If no registry exists yet, compilation runs under the [[file:glossary.org::#term/invalidation][invalidation]] lock; a second check prevents concurrent callers from compiling the same context twice. Later writes can invalidate or update this registry.

Compiles functions in [[file:glossary.org::#term/topological-order][dependency order]]: a referenced function must be available before a caller uses it. The process cache is keyed by graph structure, [[file:glossary.org::#term/base-function][base-function]] implementations, and [[file:glossary.org::#term/rich-types][rich type information]]. Types affect whether a referenced function is passed as a callable or evaluated, so different type information must not share the same compiled result.

Builds a [[file:glossary.org::#term/thunk][deferred computation]] for one argument. Values are constants; [[file:glossary.org::#term/free-argument][free arguments]] read caller input by [[file:glossary.org::#term/slot][slot]] ID with a name fallback; references use [[file:glossary.org::#term/thunk][thunks]] or delays; sequences compute their elements lazily. A base implementation therefore evaluates only the arguments it reads, which permits short-circuiting conditionals.

:PROPERTIES:

:LINE: 1563
:MINS: 2.1

An effectful primitive calls this before touching external state. It rejects an operation outside the execution's allowed effect set, then records the effect for tracing. Declaring effects for type inference is a separate responsibility; this runtime check enforces the current policy. An empty allowed set rejects every recorded effect, while nil means unrestricted execution.

* 22. ref-produces-callable?
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: executor/ref-produces-callable?
:FILE: src/graphden/executor/compile/bindings.clj
:LINE: 220
:MINS: 1.9
:END:

Distinguishes a callback from a constructor that returns a callback. A reference whose registered return type is a function type is evaluated to obtain the callable value. Other references in function-typed slots are wrapped without executing their bodies. The decision follows types and inherited return declarations, never function names. A marked callable keeps its marker in the stored type; invocation propagates that marker to its result and retains the callable's effect requirements. The [[file:../../../docs/tutorial/09-higher-order-functions.md][query constructor example]] uses this distinction to capture connection parameters in an ordinary graph.

Prepares an ordinary referenced function as a callable. The wrapper captures the current input values and execution context; its declared callback parameters receive values at each invocation. This is the runtime counterpart of ~:lambda-params~, with no separate environment object in the stored graph. Callable constructors take the evaluation path described by ~ref-produces-callable?~ instead.

Builds the name translation at a reference call. If a caller exposes an argument under a new name but the referenced function still uses its original name, the translation supplies the value under the referenced function's name. See the [[file:../../../docs/adr/ADR-inherited-rename-surface.md][inherited rename design]].

Computes aliases for inherited rename chains that reach outside the root's own [[file:glossary.org::#term/slot][slot]] set. For example, an internal reader of ~:branch-row~ can receive input exposed publicly as ~:item~. The aliases are prepared at compile time and copied into the input map at runtime; the docstring contains a worked example.
